newsitem.title: UK: Philippines to have 1996 budget surplus -minister.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to have 1996 budget surplus -minister.

text.p: The Philippines is on track for a third successive budget surplus this year, Finance Minister Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday.
He told Reuters it was too soon to raise economic growth targets for the year, despite higher-than-expected gross national product growth in the first six months.
"I'd prefer to remain on the conservative side," de Ocampo said when asked if the government would revise up its GNP target after growth rose higher than expected 7.06 percent in the first half.
But de Ocampo, in London to promote the government's planned Brady bond swap, told investors that the budget would again be in surplus.
"I have no doubt we are going to do it again in 1996," he told investors.

Also, planned tax reforms should put the country in a stronger fiscal position and provide better chances for sustainable growth as privatisation becomes a smaller part of government revenue, he said.
He noted latest inflation figures were lower than had been expected, while foreign exchange reserves had surged in recent years.
The government is planning to replace up to $1.9 billion of its Brady bonds into uncollateralised Eurobonds.

The new bonds will be a 20-year fixed rate issue, with a minimum spread of 225 basis points over 30-year U.S. Treasuries, and a 15-year floating rate issue at a minimum 175 points over six-month Libor.
The minimum size for each issue will be $200 million.
The offer closes on September 20, but bidders who do not hold Bradys will have by September 27 to show they do hold Brady bonds.
